newsitem.title: INDIA: India PM refuses to quit, Congress stakes claim.
newsitem.headline: India PM refuses to quit, Congress stakes claim.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Monday he will face parliament next month and was not planning to resign after the Congress party withdrew its make-or-break support for his 10-month old government.
A Congress official told Reuters his party had formally staked its claim before President Shankar Dayal Sharma on Monday to head a new government.
The Congress withdrew its support for the ruling United Front alliance on Sunday, accusing Deve Gowda of failing to check the growth of communalism among other reasons.

"There is no question of my resignation or suggesting dissolution of the (lower) house," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Deve Gowda as telling reporters in the capital. "The trial of strength will be held on the floor of the house."

Parliament's budget session is due to reconvene on April 21. But state television quoted L.K. Advani, president of the rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), as demanding that it should meet earlier next month.
On Sunday, Congress president Sitaram Kesri said his party was withdrawing its support for Deve Gowda's 15-party coalition government in the lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha.

"My understanding is that a formal claim has been made," the Congress official, who did not wish to be identified, told Reuters. "I cannot say if the Congress president went personally to meet the President or if a letter was sent to him."
The Congress party was expected to make a formal statement at 4:00 p.m. (1030 GMT), the official said.
Asked if he was confident he could prove his majority in the Lok Sabha, Deve Gowda said: "We will take care of it."
The news agency quoted the prime minister as saying the 15 parties in his United Front alliance were "standing together like a rock" and would decide the future course of action.

"I will abide by the decisions of the Steering Committee which is the highest policy-making body of the (United) Front," PTI quoted Deve Gowda as saying. The Steering Committee was due to meet at 3:30 p.m. (1000 GMT) on Monday.

Sources in the ruling centre-left United Front alliance told Reuters that Deve Gowda held talks with senior leaders of his coalition ahead of a meeting of its decision-making Steering Committee later on Monday.

"The prime minister was assured, and he agreed, that the United Front will continue to be in charge (of the government)," a source close to Deve Gowda said. "There is a crisis which we will overcome, without the need for mid-term elections."
Indian shares plunged more than eight percent in panicky trade on Monday as news of the Congress withdrawal of support sank in.
Bombay's benchmark stocks index crashed 299.63 points, or 8.2 percent, to a provisional close of 3,363.90.
Stockbrokers in Bombay, India's financial centre, said it was unclear how Congress, which has only 140 deputies in the 545-seat Lok Sabha, or lower house, could form a government.
Deve Gowda's alliance, which groups free-traders, communists and centrists and controls some 178 deputies in the lower house, was formed in June 1996 after inconclusive national elections.
An opinion poll last month predicted major gains for the BJP against both the United Front and the Congress if mid-term polls were held soon.
